<p><strong>Super Eagles’ trip to Nizhny Novgorod has the feel of a casting call as much as a football match, <a href="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/">Afrik-Foot</a> reports.</strong></p>



<p>When the <a href="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/super-eagles-fixtures-and-results">Super Eagles face Russia</a> on Tuesday, October 6, at the 44,000-capacity Nizhny Novgorod Stadium, <a href="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/super-eagle-eric-chelle-salary-wife-madrid">Éric Chelle</a> will have a very different squad from the one that suffered a 3-0 AFCON qualifying defeat in Guinea-Bissau. Kick-off is scheduled for 5pm Nigerian time, with Russia entering the game after a 2-0 victory over Iran in Kazan.</p>



<p>The original Super Eagles selection for the Russia clash already contained several unfamiliar faces, but the squad has changed again.</p>



<p><a href="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/wilfred-ndidi">Wilfred Ndidi,</a> Bright Osayi-Samuel and Victory Akpe have withdrawn, opening the door for teenage midfielder <a href="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/super-eagles-russia-osuji-chelle-otemewo">John Otomewo and 20-year-old centre-back Vince Osuji</a>. The updated group therefore gives Chelle a collection of players whose international reputations are still being written, from Finnish goalkeeping prospect Samuel James to Benfica forward Peter Edokpolor and Kristiansund midfielder Igor Wilfred.</p>



<p>Russia could give them their first official senior appearance for Nigeria and, more importantly, give Chelle evidence about who can survive beyond an experimental squad.</p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading">Unfamiliar Super Eagles stars to watch</h2>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Samuel James, SJK</h3>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="1672" height="941" src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA=" alt="New Super Eagles goalkeeper Samuel James" class="wp-image-934741 lazy" data-src="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/thumbor/l5TT4pyNuXVLYXC_Kzv5wWmJlm8=/1672x941/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.afrik-foot.com%2Fen-ng%2F2026%2F09%2Fdf505fc7-bca6-4374-a71d-d029fed0482a.png"><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">New Super Eagles goalkeeper Samuel James. Photo Credit: AI edit </figcaption></figure>



<p>At 20, <a href="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/samuel-james-super-eagles-nigeria-new-gk">Samuel James</a> is the tallest and most intriguing of Nigeria’s fresh goalkeeping options. The 1.95-metre SJK goalkeeper was born on April 5, 2006, and developed at Mavlon FC before moving to Finland in 2025. SJK initially placed him with its reserve side, SJK Akatemia, where he accumulated substantial Ykkösliiga experience.</p>



<p>James has since built the sort of European grounding that can accelerate a goalkeeper’s development. His first senior Nigeria invitation came specifically for the Russia friendly, and the match could become his first official appearance for the Super Eagles.</p>



<p>His physical frame, youth and regular competitive football make him a serious long-term project, although Stanley Nwabali’s presence means a starting place on Tuesday is far from guaranteed. A convincing cameo could, however, put James into Chelle’s future goalkeeper rotation.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Michael Atata, Ikorodu City</h3>



<p>Michael Atata represents the other end of the goalkeeper pathway. The 20-year-old came through the NPFL with Ikorodu City and was already attracting attention before Chelle invited him into the national setup.</p>



<p>Atata’s domestic numbers provide the strongest argument for his selection. He recorded 16 clean sheets in 31 NPFL appearances during the 2025/26 campaign, a remarkable return for a young goalkeeper competing in his first major senior environment.</p>



<p>His challenge is obvious: Nwabali and James offer stronger international or overseas experience. Yet Atata has something Chelle has repeatedly sought, evidence that a home-based player can force his way into the conversation through performance. Russia could be the night he converts that reputation into a first senior appearance.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Isaac James, Alverca</h3>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="5241" height="3496" src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA=" alt="Super Eagles invitee and Alverca star Isaac James" class="wp-image-933701 lazy" data-src="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/thumbor/86d0Pi76upmn3aV1gS3XHQenuWo=/5241x3496/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.afrik-foot.com%2Fen-ng%2F2026%2F09%2Fimago1082045882h.jpg"><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Super Eagles invitee and Alverca star Isaac James. Photo by IMAGO </figcaption></figure>



<p>Isaac James is already closer to the finished product than many of the names around him. The 22-year-old left-back has established himself in Portugal after beginning his career with Garden City Panthers before moving to Lorient in France. He developed through Lorient’s reserve system and made his first-team debut in 2024 before joining Alverca in 2025.</p>



<p>His 2026/27 start was particularly eye-catching. James started Alverca’s first seven Primeira Liga matches, accumulating 604 minutes and providing two assists. He has also played at left-back, left midfield and left-sided centre-back.</p>



<p>Nigeria already called him into the September AFCON squad, but he stayed on the bench against Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau. Russia therefore offers his clearest route to a first senior appearance. His versatility gives him one of the strongest chances among the newcomers of becoming a regular squad option.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Vince Osuji, Tromsø</h3>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="6215" height="4145" src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA=" alt="Nigerian youngster Vince Osuji" class="wp-image-929258 lazy" data-src="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/thumbor/yUKQ7uuM-lxUcuXOrg6DUjYxj78=/6215x4145/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.afrik-foot.com%2Fen-ng%2F2026%2F08%2Fimago1079867729.jpg"><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Nigerian youngster Vince Osuji. Copyright: xYannickxVerhoevenxIMAGO</figcaption></figure>



<p>Vince Osuji was not part of the original Super Eagles plan for Russia. The 20-year-old centre-back entered the squad after Akpe withdrew, arriving with a career that has accelerated through Sweden, Belgium and Norway.</p>



<p>Tromsø signed him from Club Brugge in August after he had developed at Club NXT and previously played for Kalmar FF.</p>



<p>At 1.88m, Osuji brings speed, size and the experience of senior European football despite his age. He started Tromsø’s 0-0 draw with Sarpsborg 08 on August 30 and had collected 138 Eliteserien minutes across three appearances when Chelle called.</p>



<p>His international opportunity arrived suddenly, but his club trajectory suggests he is not simply filling a vacant shirt. A strong debut could make him a genuine candidate for future defensive depth, particularly with Nigeria constantly searching for younger centre-backs capable of competing abroad.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">John Otomewo, Stade de Reims</h3>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="1024" height="597" src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA=" alt="John Otomewo signs for Stade de Reims" class="wp-image-923826 lazy" data-src="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/thumbor/30DcAutiFdCBbFhssAddi_d-SQE=/1024x597/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.afrik-foot.com%2Fen-ng%2F2026%2F07%2FSans-titre-1-2-1024x597-1.png"><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">John Otomewo signs for Stade de Reims. [Photo Credit: Reims official website].</figcaption></figure>



<p>Otomewo’s rise is arguably the most dramatic of the late additions. The 19-year-old defensive midfielder moved from Abia Comets to Gombe United, then to Hapoel Jerusalem, before Stade de Reims paid about €1.6m for him in July 2026. He signed a contract running until 2031.</p>



<p>CIES Football Observatory had previously ranked him among the top three under-21 midfielders playing outside Europe’s five major leagues. His first months in France have been quieter, with five Ligue 2 appearances and 136 minutes, all from the bench.</p>



<p>Ndidi’s withdrawal suddenly makes Otomewo more relevant. He could be the man asked to replace a legend of the position.</p>



<p>Still, his defensive instincts and ability to operate at the base of midfield give Chelle an intriguing alternative. Russia could begin the process of turning an exciting prospect into a national-team regular.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Ibraheem Mahfus Ajasa, Rostov</h3>



<p>Ibraheem Mahfus Ajasa has gone from an unfamiliar name in Russian football to a potential Super Eagles debutant in the space of a few hours.</p>



<p>The 20-year-old Rostov midfielder received a late invitation from Eric Chelle on October 4, with his Russian club confirming the call-up ahead of Tuesday’s friendly against Russia.</p>



<p>Born in Lagos on November 26, 2005, Ajasa stands 1.80m and is primarily a left winger, although he can also operate on the right. He joined Rostov in July 2025 on a contract running until June 2027 after previously playing for Egyptian club Modern Sport.</p>



<p>His senior club experience is still modest. Ajasa made his Rostov debut during the 2025/26 Russian Premier League season, coming off the bench for the final 10 minutes of a match. He has not yet accumulated a substantial first-team workload in the current campaign, making his sudden elevation into the Nigeria setup all the more striking.</p>



<p>Chelle’s decision nevertheless offers a window into what the coach sees in him. Ajasa has spent more than a year developing inside Russian football, and his familiarity with the country’s footballing environment could prove useful against a Russian side Nigeria will face in its own territory.</p>



<p>His ability to play on either flank also gives Chelle another attacking option after Bright Osayi-Samuel became the latest player to withdraw from the squad.</p>



<p>Tuesday could therefore be a particularly unusual moment for Ajasa. A debut would not make Ajasa an instant Super Eagles regular, but it could accelerate a career that is still taking shape. His immediate task is to turn a surprise invitation into evidence that he belongs at this level.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Chibuzo Nwoko, Fulham</h3>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="4032" height="2688" src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA=" alt="Fulham youngster Chibby Nwoko." class="wp-image-934427 lazy" data-src="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/thumbor/_Z_S4bZ6ZQ3ofANFNUoa7xpDQIA=/4032x2688/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.afrik-foot.com%2Fen-ng%2F2026%2F09%2Fimago1075433963h.jpg"><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Fulham youngster Chibby Nwoko. Photo by IMAGO</figcaption></figure>



<p>Chibuzo “Chibby” Nwoko arrives with one of the most unusual international stories in the squad. The 20-year-old London-born midfielder came through Chelsea before joining Fulham at Under-12 level and can operate as a six, eight or 10. His father has roots in Umuahia South, Abia State.</p>



<p>Nwoko spent the latter part of last season on loan at Forest Green Rovers, where he made 22 appearances and started 17 consecutive matches. He then returned to Fulham and made his first-team debut against AFC Wimbledon in the Carabao Cup on August 27, playing 22 minutes in a 3-0 victory.</p>



<p>He also represented England Under-18s three times in 2023, all in friendlies, before receiving his first Nigeria invitation. His ability to carry the ball, pass from deep and cover multiple midfield roles makes him one of Chelle’s most interesting long-term projects.</p>



<p>Administrative questions surrounding his international switch still need attention, but Russia offers the footballing stage he has been waiting for.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Stephen Fumen Michael, Vendsyssel</h3>



<p>Stephen Fumen Michael is only 19, yet his rise has already moved through two levels of Danish football. The central midfielder joined Vendsyssel in August 2025 and has since established himself as a senior player rather than an academy prospect.</p>



<p>His 2026/27 numbers show that progress. Michael had started nine matches and played 732 league minutes for Vendsyssel before this Russia trip, operating primarily as a defensive or central midfielder.</p>



<p>With Ndidi gone from the squad, Michael has a clearer route to minutes and a chance to convince Chelle that his development can continue at international level.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Igor Wilfred, Kristiansund</h3>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="3000" height="2000" src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA=" alt="Super Eagles invitee and Kristiansund star Wilfred Igor." class="wp-image-934866 lazy" data-src="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/thumbor/2_iWQ4cFRn_p0zXuzsHk26Y7JM0=/3000x2000/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.afrik-foot.com%2Fen-ng%2F2026%2F09%2Fimago1060814699h.jpg"><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Super Eagles invitee and Kristiansund star Wilfred Igor. Photo by IMAGO </figcaption></figure>



<p>Igor Wilfred may be one of the least familiar names in Nigeria’s squad, but his club workload gives him a strong case. The 21-year-old central midfielder has started 18 of Kristiansund’s 20 Eliteserien matches in 2026, playing 1,631 minutes. He has recorded 37 tackles, 30 interceptions and 118 recoveries.</p>



<p>Those numbers paint a picture of a midfielder comfortable with the physical and defensive demands of top-flight football. He can operate as a No. 6 or No. 8, making him particularly useful to Chelle after Nigeria lost Ndidi from the Russia squad.</p>



<p>Igor’s route to the Super Eagles has been built almost entirely through consistent club football in Norway. A composed debut against Russia could put him in the conversation whenever Chelle needs another ball-winner or deep midfielder.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Ridwan Abdulrasaq Popoola, Al Wasl</h3>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="1015" height="1549" src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA=" alt="Ridwan Popoola" class="wp-image-933802 lazy" data-src="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/thumbor/Q408j1hadvsvSlBc-8jFfXZsDz0=/1015x1549/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.afrik-foot.com%2Fen-ng%2F2026%2F09%2F25c30070-ded7-47a8-9818-940659d0c8f0.png"><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Ridwan Popoola. Photo Credit: AI edit </figcaption></figure>



<p>Ridwan Popoola’s story moves at remarkable speed. The 19-year-old defensive midfielder went from Lagos grassroots football to Hungary and then the United Arab Emirates in less than two years. He joined Kisvárda in February 2025 after playing for Lagos-based Seamoriow FC before earning a €1.6m move to Al Wasl in July 2026.</p>



<p>His first full season in Hungary produced 28 league appearances, 26 starts and 2,159 minutes. Al Wasl then quickly made him part of its midfield, with Popoola starting seven matches and accumulating 540 minutes early in the 2026/27 campaign.</p>



<p>At 1.91m, he offers Chelle considerable physical presence in front of the defence. His age means he is unlikely to become an automatic starter immediately, but his progression suggests Nigeria may have found another long-term midfield option.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Suleiman Mubarak, Slavia Prague</h3>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="5120" height="3416" src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA=" alt="Mubarak Suleiman for Slavia Prague" class="wp-image-933685 lazy" data-src="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/thumbor/BKBoQJx1iuoVJMR7ak1uUEQ4_WE=/5120x3416/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.afrik-foot.com%2Fen-ng%2F2026%2F09%2Fimago1073598975h.jpg"><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Mubarak Suleiman for Slavia Prague. CTKxPhoto/RadekxPetrasekxImago</figcaption></figure>



<p>Suleiman Mubarak is one of the youngest names in the squad at 19. The midfielder joined Slavia Prague in 2025 from Nigerian academy Rigt 2 Win after impressing during a trial that included training with the Czech club’s first team.</p>



<p>He initially developed with Slavia’s B team before making his senior-team debut against Mladá Boleslav, where he also scored his first goal. He followed that with an assist against Karviná.</p>



<p>Mubarak’s development is still at an early stage, but exposure to a club competing at the top end of Czech football gives him a valuable platform. Russia could be the first step towards a senior midfield role.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Peter Edokpolor, Benfica</h3>





<p>Peter Edokpolor brings the prestige of Benfica but not yet the first-team status associated with the Portuguese giants. The 19-year-old forward joined Benfica from Galadima FC in 2024 and is preparing for his third season at the club.</p>



<p>His 2025/26 campaign showed genuine progress. Edokpolor played 35 matches across Benfica B, the Under-23 side, the Liga Portugal 2, the Liga Revelação and the Premier League International Cup, scoring six goals. He began the season with the Under-23s and finished with Benfica B.</p>



<p>A 1.92m centre-forward who can also play from the left, Edokpolor offers physical presence and mobility in an attack that lacks Victor Osimhen and Ademola Lookman. His first Super Eagles appearance would be less about immediate stardom and more about showing Chelle that Benfica’s latest Nigerian prospect can handle senior international football.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Umar Abubakar, Famalicão</h3>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="4500" height="3000" src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA=" alt="Umar Abubakar of FC Famalicao." class="wp-image-929928 lazy" data-src="https://www.afrik-foot.com/en-ng/thumbor/t2aDhKvZvHUloLQz8oXrYoPHrvY=/4500x3000/smart/filters:format(webp)/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.afrik-foot.com%2Fen-ng%2F2026%2F08%2Fimago1073177120.jpg"><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Umar Abubakar of FC Famalicao. Copyright: ImagoxSofiaxGarridox</figcaption></figure>



<p>Umar Abubakar’s numbers from Belgium explain why Nigeria is interested. The 20-year-old striker joined Famalicão from Nigerian academy Footwork FC after scoring 21 goals in 27 appearances for Jong Gent during the 2024/25 season. That prolific campaign earned him the Belgian club’s youth Player of the Season award before Famalicão signed him in July 2025.</p>



<p>His first Primeira Liga season produced three goals in 22 appearances, with 414 minutes, while his opportunities have been more limited in 2026/27. He had made six league appearances before the Russia camp.</p>



<p>Abubakar has already proved he can score heavily at youth level, but regular first-team football in Portugal is the next hurdle. A lively international debut could accelerate that development and give Chelle another young striking option.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Abdullahi Umar, Hradec Králové</h3>



<p>Abdullahi Umar is another 19-year-old forward whose career has suddenly moved into European competition. The Nigerian striker joined Czech club Hradec Králové in May 2026 on a contract running until 2031 and has already featured in Europa League and Conference League qualifying.</p>



<p>His European adventure has included appearances against Beşiktaş, Panathinaikos and Tromsø, while he has also been used regularly from the bench in the Czech league. He scored twice across Hradec’s two Conference League qualifying meetings with Panathinaikos and had accumulated more than 200 minutes across competitions by September.</p>



<p>At 1.91m, Umar gives Nigeria another physically imposing young forward. His lack of senior international experience makes Tuesday a major opportunity, while his exposure to European competition suggests he is already learning how to handle pressure beyond domestic football.<br></p>
